Instruction-tuned models may differ from base models (an informative comparison but limits universality). Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: counterfactual_dual_meaning_belief
Title: Two Worlds at Once: Do LLMs Internally Hold Both the Supposed and the Backgrounded-Factual Meaning of a Counterfactual?
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the canonical psycholinguistic 'dual meaning' of counterfactual conditionals (a subjunctive like 'If Tom had studied, he would have passed' conveys BOTH a supposed dependency AND the backgrounded fact that Tom did NOT study and failed), an LLM processing a counterfactual simultaneously maintains two internally-decodable belief layers about the same proposition: the SUPPOSED belief (P holds in the counterfactual world) and the BACKGROUNDED-FACTUAL belief (P is actually false). These two layers are separately linearly decodable, largely orthogonal, and causally dissociable: which layer dominates the model's downstream answer can be steered, and failures to maintain the factual layer produce a characteristic error (treating the counterfactual antecedent as actually true).
Related Work: Cognitive/psycholinguistic work robustly establishes counterfactual DUAL MEANING: subjunctive-counterfactuals express a supposition while implying the opposite factual state of affairs (Understanding Counterfactuality: A Review, Kulakova & Nieuwland 2016, 119 citations; Marking the counterfactual: ERP evidence for pragmatic processing of German subjunctives 2014, 48 citations). In LLM interpretability, 'Counterfactual reasoning: in-context emergence' (2025) finds a latent concept is linearly encoded with noise-abduction heads, and the 'Competition of Mechanisms' line (Ortu et al. 2024; reproductions 2025) traces how factual-recall vs. in-context counterfactual tokens compete, localizing factual/counterfactual info to subject/attribute positions and attention heads. Truth-probe work isolates a single linear truth direction (Geometry of Truth 2023; Truth-value judgment 2024). CRITICALLY, the competition-of-mechanisms work treats fact vs. counterfactual as a WINNER-TAKE-ALL competition for the output token and does NOT ask whether the model concurrently maintains TWO belief layers (supposed AND backgrounded-factual) about the SAME proposition, as human dual-meaning theory predicts; nor does it isolate these as separately decodable, orthogonal, steerable channels, nor connect the loss of the factual layer to the specific error of endorsing a false antecedent. My prior suppositional_belief_gating proposal concerns a binary endorsed-vs-entertained framing flag; this proposal is specifically about the two CO-PRESENT belief layers that are the signature of counterfactual conditionals. We transfer a canonical cognitive-science phenomenon (counterfactual dual meaning) into LLM belief internals with a mechanistic, causal treatment.
Abstract: When we say 'If the dice had been rigged, the game would have been unfair,' we simultaneously entertain a hypothetical world (rigged dice, unfair game) AND signal a fact about the real world (the dice were NOT rigged, the game WAS fair). Decades of psycholinguistics establish this counterfactual 'dual meaning' as a hallmark of human comprehension. LLMs increasingly reason under counterfactual premises (planning, causal reasoning, hypotheticals, safety scenarios), yet it is unknown whether they preserve both layers or collapse into one. We ask a sharp mechanistic question: when an LLM reads a counterfactual conditional, does it internally maintain TWO separable belief layers about the antecedent proposition P — a SUPPOSED belief (P holds, in the counterfactual world) and a BACKGROUNDED-FACTUAL belief (P is actually false)? We hypothesize both layers are (i) separately linearly decodable from residual-stream activations, (ii) largely orthogonal, and (iii) causally dissociable, such that steering can shift which layer governs downstream answers, and that incomplete maintenance of the factual layer produces a characteristic error — treating the false antecedent as actually true. We build a controlled dataset of counterfactual conditionals, matched indicative/factual and simple-suppositional frames, and synthetic-entity items to control priors, plus factual-inference probes ('In reality, is P true?') and consequent-inference probes. On frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B) we train linear probes for the supposed and factual layers, measure their geometry, localize the responsible heads via activation patching (comparing to competition-of-mechanisms heads), and test causal steering. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle, projected-out decodability, layer-dominance shift under steering, patching effect sizes, factual-endorsement error rate, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Generate ~6k items each anchored on a proposition P and rendered in matched frames: (a) COUNTERFACTUAL subjunctive ('If P had been the case, then Q would have happened' — implying NOT-P in reality); (b) INDICATIVE/FACTUAL control ('P is the case, so Q happens'); (c) SIMPLE-SUPPOSITION control ('Suppose P; then Q' — open supposition, no factual implication about P). Two tracks: (i) REAL propositions the model can evaluate; (ii) a SYNTHETIC novel-entity track (e.g., 'If Zorblax had orbited Kelvath, ...') with stipulated ground truth to control pretraining priors. Add probes: a FACTUAL-INFERENCE probe ('In reality, is P true?' — correct answer for counterfactuals is NO), a SUPPOSED/CONSEQUENT-INFERENCE probe ('Within the described scenario, does Q hold?'), and comprehension checks. Apply paraphrase/mood-cue perturbations to guard against surface-cue artifacts (e.g., 'had'/'would'). Human-validate a sample. 2) Two-layer probing: For Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, extract residual-stream and per-head activations at the antecedent P tokens across layers, WITHOUT asking a question. Train linear probes for (A) SUPPOSED belief in P (P holds in the counterfactual world) and (B) BACKGROUNDED-FACTUAL belief in P (P is actually false), anchored using the indicative-factual and simple-supposition frames plus reality-only items, with shuffled-label control tasks; report per-layer accuracy/AUROC. 3) Geometry / co-presence (key test): Test that in the COUNTERFACTUAL condition BOTH layers are simultaneously decodable (supposed-P high AND factual-P low), unlike the indicative frame (both align) or a hallucinated-fact frame. Compute cosine/subspace angle between the supposed and factual directions; test whether the factual layer remains decodable after projecting out the supposed layer (and vice versa) to establish separability. Track per-layer emergence of each layer (does the factual/backgrounded layer arise later, mirroring pragmatic processing?). 4) Predictiveness: Collect behavioral factual-endorsement errors (model wrongly says P is actually true, i.e., collapses to the supposed layer). Test whether the internal strength of the backgrounded-factual layer (read before query) predicts per-item correct factual inference via AUROC, beyond a log-prob baseline and beyond surface features. 5) Localization: Use activation patching / causal mediation to find heads/layers carrying each layer, and those whose weakening collapses the factual layer into the supposed one (patch counterfactual activations into indicative runs and vice versa); compare to the factual/counterfactual competition heads and subject/attribute positions from Ortu et al. and noise-abduction heads from counterfactual-emergence work. 6) Causal control: Derive contrastive steering directions for each layer (counterfactual-supposed vs. factual activations). Test (a) amplifying the supposed layer / suppressing the factual layer increases false-antecedent endorsement (the model treats the counterfactual premise as real); (b) amplifying the factual layer restores correct factual inference while preserving in-scenario consequent reasoning; (c) specificity: random-direction and truth-direction steering do not selectively move layer dominance, and consequent-inference within the scenario is preserved when appropriate; (d) collateral checks on general benchmarks (MMLU subset), indicative-frame accuracy, and perplexity. 7) Generalization: Test probe/steering transfer across counterfactual types (past/present subjunctive, nested counterfactuals), real vs. synthetic tracks, and mood-cue phrasings. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, dual-layer co-presence rate, subspace angle and projected-out decodability, per-layer emergence curves, factual-inference prediction AUROC (vs. log-prob and surface baselines), patching logit-difference effect sizes, layer-dominance shift and false-antecedent-endorsement deltas under steering, specificity checks, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The 'supposed' and 'backgrounded-factual' layers may be hard to separate cleanly because both concern the same proposition P; the matched indicative/simple-supposition frames, synthetic-entity track, and probes anchored on frames where the two layers agree vs. diverge are designed to dissociate them, and projected-out analyses quantify any residual entanglement (which is itself informative). The dual layers might not be genuinely co-present internally — the model may simply implement a winner-take-all competition (as the competition-of-mechanisms work suggests) collapsing to one belief; a robust negative result (no separable factual layer during counterfactual processing) would itself be a valuable, publishable finding contrasting LLM processing with human dual-meaning comprehension and sharpening the competition-of-mechanisms picture. The layers could be decoded via surface mood cues ('had'/'would') rather than abstract belief representations; paraphrase/mood perturbations, comprehension checks, and the synthetic track mitigate this. Belief may not be cleanly linearly decodable at every layer; we report layerwise results with control tasks. The responsible components may be distributed rather than discrete heads; we treat 'steer to shift layer dominance / restore factual inference' as the causal test rather than pinning exact heads. Steering could degrade fluency or destroy the model's ability to reason within the counterfactual scenario (over-suppressing the supposed layer); we use small magnitudes, random/truth-direction baselines, and monitor perplexity, consequent-inference accuracy, indicative-frame accuracy, and general benchmarks. Human dual-meaning comparison is structural, not a claim of identical mechanism. Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: defeasibility_flag_belief
Title: Rule or Rule-of-Thumb? An Internal Defeasibility Flag That Gates How a Single Counterexample Revises an LLM's Belief
Short Hypothesis: LLMs internally tag a general belief about a category as either DEFEASIBLE (a default/generic that tolerates exceptions, e.g. 'birds fly') or STRICT (an exception-intolerant universal, e.g. 'all bachelors are unmarried'). This defeasibility flag is (i) linearly decodable from residual-stream activations, (ii) largely orthogonal to the truth-value direction, and (iii) causally gates counterexample-driven revision: presenting a single exception should collapse belief in a strict universal but only mildly dent belief in a defeasible generic; steering the flag reverses this asymmetry, and mis-flagging predicts the two canonical human/LLM errors (misreading generics as universals -> overgeneralization; and unstable beliefs that overreact to one exception).
Related Work: Behavioral work robustly shows LLMs mishandle generics and defeasible reasoning: they conflate generics with universals and overgeneralize (Penguins Don't Fly 2022; Exceptions, Instantiations, and Overgeneralization 2024), fail to maintain stable beliefs when exceptions or irrelevant facts are added (Are LLMs classical or nonmonotonic reasoners? 2024), and vary widely on 20 defeasible patterns with CoT often hurting (Generics and Default Reasoning in LLMs 2025); MLMs are insensitive to quantification yet encode a generic-form meaning (Interpretation of Generalization in MLMs 2023). Classic interpretability isolates a linear truth-value direction (Geometry of Truth 2023; Truth-value judgment 2024). CRITICALLY, all defeasibility/generics work is behavioral or about quantifier probabilities; none isolate an internal DEFEASIBILITY flag (defeasible-default vs. strict-universal) as a decodable variable distinct from truth-value, nor test whether it causally gates how a single counterexample revises the belief. This differs from my prior essentialist_belief_mutability proposal, which tags a specific instance's property as essential vs. accidental; here the axis is the LOGICAL FORM of a general belief (exception-tolerant generic vs. exception-intolerant universal) and its role in counterexample-driven, non-monotonic revision. We transfer a canonical non-monotonic-reasoning phenomenon into LLM belief internals with a mechanistic, causal treatment.
Abstract: 'Birds fly' and 'all squares have four sides' look grammatically similar but behave differently under a counterexample: a penguin leaves the first belief essentially intact, while a single three-sided 'square' would destroy the second. Humans track this difference (defeasible generics vs. strict universals), and LLMs are notorious for confusing them - overgeneralizing generics into universals, or letting one exception (or even an irrelevant fact) destabilize a belief. We ask a mechanistic question: does an LLM internally represent whether a general belief is defeasible or strict, and does that representation govern how a counterexample revises it? We hypothesize that a 'defeasibility' flag is (i) linearly decodable from residual-stream activations, (ii) largely orthogonal to the truth-value direction, and (iii) causally gates counterexample-driven revision - so that beliefs internally tagged strict collapse under one exception while those tagged defeasible barely move, and steering the flag reverses this asymmetry. We build a controlled dataset of general claims labeled defeasible (generics) vs. strict (analytic/definitional universals), matched in surface form, plus a synthetic-category track that stipulates a rule's logical form in-context to control priors, each paired with a single counterexample. On frozen open-weight models (Llama-3, Qwen2.5, Gemma-2, Mistral) we train linear probes to decode defeasibility vs. truth, measure their geometry, quantify a per-item revision-plasticity gap under a counterexample, test whether internal mis-flagging predicts overgeneralization and instability errors, localize the responsible heads via activation patching, and test causal steering. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle, projected-out decodability, counterexample-revision gap, error-prediction AUROC, patching effect sizes, post-steering plasticity reversal, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Generate ~6k general claims labeled by LOGICAL FORM: (a) DEFEASIBLE generics that tolerate exceptions ('Birds fly', 'Dogs have four legs', 'Metals conduct electricity'), (b) STRICT universals that do not ('All squares have four sides', 'All bachelors are unmarried', 'Every prime greater than 2 is odd'). Balance across domains (biology, artifacts, math/definitions, social) and MATCH surface form where possible (bare-plural generics vs. explicitly-quantified universals, and paraphrases that swap 'birds fly' <-> 'all birds fly' to test form vs. cue). Two tracks: (i) REAL claims; (ii) a SYNTHETIC novel-category track that stipulates a rule's form in-context ('Every zorb is by definition three-eyed [strict]' vs. 'Zorbs typically have three eyes [defeasible]'), controlling pretraining priors and dissociating form from lexical triggers. For each claim, construct a matched SINGLE-COUNTEREXAMPLE ('You encounter a bird that cannot fly' / 'You encounter a square with three sides'), plus an IRRELEVANT-FACT control ('Lions have manes') and a SUPPORTING-INSTANCE control ('Owls fly'). Add a behavioral REVISION probe (does the model retract/weaken the general claim after the counterexample?) and comprehension checks (can it restate the claim's form); apply paraphrase/format perturbations. Human-validate defeasible/strict labels on a sample. 2) Probing: For Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, extract residual-stream and per-head activations at the claim tokens across layers. Train logistic-regression probes for (i) TRUTH-VALUE (true vs. false general claims) and (ii) DEFEASIBILITY (defeasible-generic vs. strict-universal), with shuffled-label control tasks; report per-layer accuracy/AUROC. 3) Geometry: Compute cosine/subspace angle between the defeasibility and truth-value directions; test whether defeasibility remains decodable after projecting out truth (and vice versa) to establish orthogonality, and whether the direction generalizes across real and synthetic tracks and across surface-matched paraphrases. 4) Counterexample-revision gap (key test): Present each true general claim, then its single counterexample, and measure (a) internal belief change via the truth probe and (b) behavioral retraction. Define per-item plasticity. Prediction: STRICT universals show large belief collapse under one counterexample (correct) while DEFEASIBLE generics show only mild denting (correct); mis-behavior appears as generics collapsing like universals (instability) or universals resisting (over-rigidity). Also test the IRRELEVANT-FACT and SUPPORTING-INSTANCE controls: a well-behaved model should not revise a generic given either, reproducing/dissociating the human 'unstable belief' finding. 5) Predictiveness: Test whether the internal defeasibility readout (read before the counterexample) predicts per-item overgeneralization errors (treating a generic as universal in a downstream 'does it hold for ALL?' probe) and instability errors (revising a generic given irrelevant/supporting info), via AUROC beyond a log-prob baseline and beyond surface lexical features. 6) Localization: Use activation patching / causal mediation to find heads/layers carrying the defeasibility signal and gating counterexample revision (patch defeasible-claim activations into strict-claim runs and vice versa at the counterexample point; find the minimal component that flips revision behavior); compare to truth/belief heads. 7) Causal control: Derive a contrastive 'defeasibility' steering direction (defeasible vs. strict activations, controlling for truth). Test (a) steering strict claims toward 'defeasible' makes them resist the counterexample (over-tolerant); (b) steering generics toward 'strict' makes one counterexample collapse them (over-brittle); (c) specificity: random-direction and truth-direction steering do not selectively move revision, and the model's factual belief is preserved; (d) collateral checks on general benchmarks (MMLU subset), non-manipulated accuracy, and perplexity. Test whether steering toward the CORRECT form improves calibrated revision. 8) Generalization: Test probe/steering transfer across domains, real vs. synthetic tracks, and quantifier-explicit vs. bare-generic phrasings. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle and projected-out decodability vs. truth, counterexample-revision plasticity gap (strict vs. defeasible; internal and behavioral), overgeneralization/instability error-prediction AUROC (vs. log-prob and lexical baselines), patching logit-difference effect sizes, post-steering plasticity reversal and specificity, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Revision behavior could be driven by the claim's pretraining confidence rather than a distinct defeasibility flag; the synthetic novel-category track (form stipulated in-context, decoupled from prior strength), surface-matched paraphrases, and conditioning error-prediction on a confidence baseline are designed to dissociate defeasibility from raw confidence. The flag may be entangled with surface cues (bare plural vs. 'all'/'every', 'by definition' vs. 'typically'); we mitigate with paraphrase perturbations, comprehension checks, and the synthetic track where cues are balanced. Defeasibility and truth directions may be less orthogonal than hypothesized, in which case the finding characterizes their entanglement (still informative). The defeasible/strict label is partly graded/subjective (some generics are near-universal); we human-validate and treat borderline items separately. The effect may be absent internally - a robust negative result (LLMs' behavioral generic/universal confusion is NOT backed by an internal defeasibility representation gating revision) is itself a valuable, publishable finding constraining the generics-in-LLMs literature. Probes may not be cleanly linear at every layer; we report layerwise results with control tasks. The gating component may be distributed; we treat 'steer to reverse/calibrate plasticity' as the causal test rather than pinning an exact head. Behavioral retraction/overgeneralization scoring on open-ended output needs an LLM-judge plus human validation. Steering could degrade fluency or make the model indiscriminately rigid or labile; we use small magnitudes, random/truth-direction baselines, and monitor perplexity, non-manipulated accuracy, and general benchmarks. Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: transitive_belief_leakage
Title: Does Belief Survive the Chain? Probing Whether LLMs Propagate Uncertainty Across Inferential Steps or Leak Certainty Into Their Conclusions
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM internally derives a conclusion C from a chain of individually-uncertain premises (A≈p1, A→B≈p2, B→C≈p3), a rational agent's belief in C should be BOUNDED by (and roughly the product of) the link beliefs, degrading as the chain lengthens. We hypothesize LLMs instead exhibit 'certainty leakage': the internally-decoded belief in the conclusion is systematically HIGHER than the product of the internally-decoded link beliefs and decays far more slowly than probability theory dictates as chain length grows — an internal over-propagation of certainty that is decodable, predicts long-chain overconfidence errors, and is carried by an identifiable component that can be steered to restore proper uncertainty attenuation.
Related Work: Prior work shows LLM internal beliefs skew CoT via confirmation bias (Unveiling Confirmation Bias in CoT 2025), that internal consistency across layers signals reasoning reliability (Calibrating Reasoning with Internal Consistency 2024), that multi-hop reasoning activates a distribution of intermediate answers in middle layers (Distributional Reasoning in LLMs 2024), and that belief/truth directions are linearly decodable and context-sensitive causal mediators of in-context inference (Truth-value judgment 2024; Language Models with Rationality/REFLEX 2023 for belief-graph consistency). Behavioral work on incoherent probability judgments and the conjunction fallacy (my prior internal_belief_coherence_gap) concerns STATIC conjunctions P(A∧B) at a single query, not inferential chains. Belief-manifold work (Shape of Beliefs 2026) shows posteriors' mean/variance are encoded but studies single-distribution updating, not multi-step deductive propagation. CRITICALLY, no prior work asks whether an LLM's INTERNAL belief in a DERIVED conclusion respects the multiplicative attenuation of uncertainty across a chain of uncertain premises, whether certainty LEAKS (conclusion believed more than the weakest/product of links warrants), how this scales with CHAIN LENGTH, or whether an identifiable component can be steered to restore attenuation. We reframe long-chain reasoning overconfidence as an internal uncertainty-propagation failure and give it a mechanistic, causal treatment, distinct from static-coherence, confirmation-bias, and layerwise-consistency work.
Abstract: A rational reasoner who is only 80% sure of each of five inferential steps should be far less than 80% sure of the final conclusion — uncertainty compounds along a chain. Yet LLMs are notorious for stating long derivations with unwarranted confidence. Prior interpretability work shows internal beliefs are linearly decodable and shape chain-of-thought, but none ask whether the model's INTERNAL belief in a derived conclusion respects the multiplicative attenuation of uncertainty across the chain that produced it. We hypothesize 'certainty leakage': the internally-decoded belief in a conclusion C is systematically higher than the product of the internally-decoded beliefs in its constituent links, and decays far more slowly than probability theory dictates as chain length grows. We further hypothesize that (i) both link-beliefs and conclusion-belief are linearly decodable, (ii) the leakage magnitude grows with chain length and predicts long-chain reasoning errors, and (iii) it is carried by an identifiable component such that steering it restores proper attenuation, improving calibration on long chains without harming short ones. We build controlled inference-chain items where each link's belief strength is stipulated (via explicit likelihood-ratio-style premises and a synthetic-entity track to control priors) and chain length is varied from 1 to 6. On frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B) we train linear belief probes to read each link-belief and the conclusion-belief, compute a per-item leakage score against the product baseline, trace its length-scaling, localize the responsible heads via activation patching, and test causal control by steering. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, leakage magnitude vs. product baseline, length-decay slope vs. rational, leakage–error AUROC, patching effect sizes, post-steering attenuation restoration and calibration gains, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Generate ~5k inferential-chain items where a conclusion C follows from a chain of links (A; A→B; B→C; ...) of controllable length L in {1,2,3,4,5,6}. Each link is assigned an explicit belief strength (e.g., 'usually/probably/possibly' calibrated to stipulated probabilities, or explicit '80% of the time' framings) so a rational product-of-links belief in C is computable. Two tracks: (a) REAL commonsense/factual chains; (b) a SYNTHETIC novel-entity track (invented entities/relations, e.g., 'Most zorbs are vantar; most vantar glow; so this zorb glows') with fully stipulated link probabilities to control pretraining priors and give an exact rational conclusion belief. Include matched conditions varying only chain length while holding the weakest-link strength constant, plus a CERTAIN-CHAIN control (all links = ~1.0, where the conclusion SHOULD stay high) to dissociate leakage from generic length/context decay. Add a behavioral CONCLUSION-CONFIDENCE probe ('How confident are you that C? Rate 0-100'), comprehension checks (can the model restate each link's strength), and paraphrase/order perturbations. 2) Belief probing: For Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, extract residual-stream and per-head activations at each LINK proposition's tokens and at the CONCLUSION proposition's tokens across layers. Train a linear/graded BELIEF-STRENGTH probe (regressing a calibrated belief score, anchored on single-premise items with known stipulated probabilities and shuffled-label control tasks); report per-layer accuracy/R^2. Read the internal belief for each link and for the conclusion WITHOUT asking the confidence question. 3) Leakage measurement (key test): Define per-item leakage = internal conclusion-belief minus the product (and minus the min, the weakest-link) of internal link-beliefs. Test leakage > 0 (conclusion over-believed relative to the product/weakest link) across models and tracks versus the rational-attenuation null; confirm the CERTAIN-CHAIN control shows no spurious decay so that any leakage in uncertain chains is not a length artifact. 4) Length scaling: Fit conclusion-belief vs. chain length L for uncertain chains and compare the internal decay slope to the rational product decay slope; the leakage prediction is a much flatter internal decay (certainty over-propagated) than probability theory dictates. Compare verbal-output decay to internal decay. 5) Predictiveness: Collect behavioral long-chain errors (the model asserts a conclusion that does not actually follow with the stated confidence, or errs on the synthetic ground-truth). Test whether internal leakage (read before the query) predicts per-item long-chain overconfidence errors via AUROC, beyond a log-prob baseline and beyond chain length itself. 6) Localization: Use activation patching / causal mediation to find heads/layers that carry the conclusion-belief and inflate it above the product of links (patch short-chain vs. long-chain conclusion activations, and patch weak-link activations into the conclusion representation; find the minimal component that lowers/raises conclusion-belief toward the product); compare to belief/truth heads (Truth-value judgment) and the middle-layer intermediate-answer distribution (Distributional Reasoning). 7) Causal control: Derive a contrastive 'certainty-leakage' steering direction (leaky vs. properly-attenuated conclusion activations). Test (a) subtracting it lowers conclusion-belief toward the product-of-links / rational value on uncertain chains and improves calibration/accuracy on long chains; (b) adding it exaggerates over-propagation; (c) specificity: random-direction and truth-direction steering do not selectively restore attenuation, and CERTAIN-CHAIN conclusions (which should stay high) are preserved; (d) collateral checks on general benchmarks (MMLU subset), short-chain accuracy, and perplexity. 8) Generalization: Test probe/steering transfer across real vs. synthetic tracks, chain lengths, and link-strength distributions. Metrics: probe accuracy/R^2, leakage magnitude vs. product and weakest-link baselines, internal-vs-rational length-decay slopes, internal-vs-verbal gap, leakage–error AUROC (vs. log-prob and chain-length baselines), patching logit-difference effect sizes, post-steering attenuation restoration, calibration (ECE) and long-chain accuracy deltas, certain-chain specificity, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The graded belief-strength probe is harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe; miscalibration could bias the leakage estimate. We mitigate by anchoring on single-premise items with known stipulated probabilities, reporting layerwise results with control tasks, and focusing on the RELATIVE comparison between conclusion-belief and the product/weakest-link of internally-decoded link-beliefs (a within-representation contrast that does not require absolute calibration). Apparent leakage could reflect the model using additional valid evidence for C beyond the stated chain (real track); the SYNTHETIC novel-entity track with fully stipulated link probabilities isolates chain-only propagation. Slow decay with length could be a generic context-retention artifact rather than certainty over-propagation; the CERTAIN-CHAIN control (which should stay high) and the length-matched weakest-link-constant condition dissociate genuine leakage from length effects. The effect may be absent internally — a robust negative result (LLMs internally attenuate uncertainty appropriately, and overconfidence is only a verbalization artifact) would itself be a valuable, publishable finding. Reading belief at 'link' vs. 'conclusion' tokens is imperfect since positions differ; we anchor probes at matched proposition tokens and use paraphrase perturbations. The leakage component may be distributed rather than a discrete head; we treat 'steer to restore attenuation' as the causal test rather than pinning an exact head. Steering could degrade fluency or make the model indiscriminately under-confident on valid chains; we use small magnitudes, random/truth-direction baselines, and monitor perplexity, short-chain and certain-chain accuracy, and general benchmarks. Long-chain error scoring on open-ended output needs an LLM-judge plus human validation on a sample. Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: recognition_truth_leak
Title: It Feels Familiar, So It Must Be True: A Recognition-to-Truth Leak in LLM Beliefs
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human recognition-based truth effect (statements that merely feel recognized are judged truer, an effect that outweighs actual repetition), an LLM's internally-decoded belief in a claim's TRUTH is inflated by its internal FAMILIARITY/RECOGNITION signal for the claim's entity, independent of (and even against) whether the model actually knows the relevant fact. This recognition-to-truth leak is linearly decodable, largely orthogonal to whether the fact is genuinely known, predicts familiarity-driven hallucination, and is carried by an identifiable component that can be steered to decouple recognition from truth.
Related Work: Human research establishes a recognition-based truth effect: statements JUDGED old (recognized) receive higher truth ratings, and this effect exceeds the effect of actual factual repetition (Recognition-based truth effect 2023); prospective feeling-of-knowing (FOK) is dissociable from actual knowledge and can rest on mere cue-familiarity rather than target-accessibility (FOK & partial knowledge 2016; metacognitive domain specificity 2020). In LLM interpretability, sparse-autoencoder 'entity recognition / knowledge-awareness' directions detect whether the model recognizes an entity and causally gate refusal/hallucination (Do I Know This Entity? 2024); 'factual self-awareness' linear features predict correct recall (Factual Self-Awareness 2025); internal states encode the knowledge-RECALL PROCESS, not truthfulness, so associated hallucinations look like facts (LLMs Do NOT Know What They Don't Know 2025); and truth is linearly decodable (Geometry of Truth 2023). CRITICALLY, none ask whether the RECOGNITION/FAMILIARITY signal CONTAMINATES the TRUTH judgment — whether merely recognizing an entity inflates the internally-decoded belief that a claim about it is true, independent of actual knowledge. Prior recognition work links recognition to refusal/hallucination-likelihood, not to a truth-inflation bias; my prior illusory-truth proposal concerns IN-CONTEXT repetition, whereas here the source is PARAMETRIC recognition/familiarity. We transfer the canonical recognition-based truth effect into LLM belief internals with a mechanistic, causal treatment.
Abstract: People rate statements they merely recognize as truer, even when recognition carries no diagnostic information — a recognition-based truth effect that can outweigh the effect of genuine repetition, and a cousin of the feeling-of-knowing that rests on cue-familiarity rather than real knowledge. LLMs are known to encode an entity-recognition signal (whether they 'know' a subject) and a separate truth signal, and to hallucinate confidently about familiar-but-unknown entities. We ask a sharper, mechanistic question: does the model's recognition/familiarity signal leak into and inflate its belief in a claim's truth, independent of whether it actually knows the relevant fact? We hypothesize that (i) an entity-recognition/familiarity channel and a truth channel are separately linearly decodable, (ii) the recognition channel contaminates the truth channel — claims about recognized entities are internally believed truer, holding actual knowledge constant — an internal signature of the recognition-based truth effect, (iii) the leak is graded with familiarity and largest when the model recognizes the entity but lacks the specific fact, predicting familiarity-driven (associated) hallucination, and (iv) the leak is carried by an identifiable component that can be steered to decouple recognition from truth. We build a controlled dataset crossing entity FAMILIARITY (recognized/popular vs. unrecognized/rare, plus synthetic entities) with claim VERACITY (true/false) and KNOWLEDGE status (fact actually known vs. not). On frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B) we train linear probes to decode recognition, truth, and knowledge, measure their geometry, quantify a per-claim recognition-to-truth leak, test its predictiveness for hallucination, localize the responsible heads via activation patching, and test causal steering. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle, projected-out decodability, leak magnitude, leak–hallucination AUROC, patching effect sizes, post-steering decoupling, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Generate ~6k subject-relation-attribute claims crossing three factors. (A) ENTITY FAMILIARITY: highly-recognized/popular entities (frequent in pretraining), low-familiarity/rare real entities, and fully SYNTHETIC novel entities (never seen) to anchor the unrecognized end. (B) CLAIM VERACITY: true vs. false attribute claims. (C) KNOWLEDGE status: whether the model actually knows the correct attribute (measured empirically by closed-book accuracy). Crucially include the diagnostic RECOGNIZED-BUT-UNKNOWN cell (familiar entity, but the specific fact is not reliably recalled) versus RECOGNIZED-AND-KNOWN and UNRECOGNIZED cells. Use subject-popularity/frequency estimates to set familiarity, and match claim surface form across familiarity levels (paraphrase/format perturbations) to guard against lexical confounds. Add a behavioral TRUTH-JUDGMENT probe ('Is this claim true? + confidence') and comprehension checks. Human-validate a sample. 2) Three-channel probing: For Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, extract residual-stream and per-head activations at the entity/attribute tokens across layers, WITHOUT asking the truth question. Following prior entity-recognition and truth-probe methods, train linear probes for (R) RECOGNITION/FAMILIARITY (recognized vs. unrecognized entity), (T) TRUTH-VALUE (true vs. false claim), and (K) KNOWLEDGE (will the model correctly recall this fact), with shuffled-label control tasks; report per-layer accuracy/AUROC. 3) Geometry: Compute cosine/subspace angle between the recognition, truth, and knowledge directions; test whether truth remains decodable after projecting out recognition (and vice versa), and whether recognition is distinct from the genuine-knowledge direction, to characterize the leak's source. 4) Recognition-to-truth leak (key test): Define per-claim leak = shift of the internal truth readout toward 'true' as a function of entity recognition, holding knowledge and veracity constant (comparing recognized-but-unknown vs. unrecognized cells for matched FALSE claims). Test leak > 0 across models versus a recognition-independent null; confirm the strongest leak in the RECOGNIZED-BUT-UNKNOWN cell (familiarity without diagnostic knowledge), mirroring the human cue-familiarity FOK. Replicate the human finding that recognition's effect on internal truth exceeds a matched in-context-repetition manipulation. Compare internal leak to stated truth judgments (behavioral recognition-based truth effect). 5) Predictiveness: Test whether the internal leak (read before any query) predicts familiarity-driven associated hallucination (confidently asserting a false attribute about a recognized entity) via AUROC, beyond a log-prob baseline and beyond the knowledge probe. 6) Localization: Use activation patching / causal mediation to find heads/layers that transport the recognition signal into the truth channel (patch recognized-entity activations into unrecognized-entity runs and vice versa; find the minimal component that raises/lowers the truth readout); compare to entity-recognition SAE directions and truth/belief heads from prior work. 7) Causal control: Derive a contrastive 'recognition-to-truth leak' steering direction (recognized vs. unrecognized activations, controlling for knowledge). Test (a) subtracting it decouples recognition from truth — lowering unwarranted belief in false claims about recognized entities and reducing associated hallucination; (b) amplifying it exaggerates the leak; (c) specificity: random-direction and truth-direction steering do not selectively decouple, and genuine-knowledge recall is preserved; (d) collateral checks on general benchmarks (MMLU subset), known-fact accuracy, and perplexity. 8) Generalization: Test probe/steering transfer across entity types (people, places, works, organizations), familiarity levels, and real vs. synthetic entities. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle and projected-out decodability, recognition-to-truth leak magnitude and sign, recognition-vs-repetition comparison, internal-vs-verbal gap, leak–hallucination AUROC (vs. log-prob and knowledge baselines), patching logit-difference effect sizes, post-steering decoupling and specificity, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The leak could reflect legitimate inference (claims about popular entities are, on average, more likely to be true in training data) rather than a spurious recognition-to-truth contamination; the FALSE-claim cells (where recognition and truth diverge), the matched RECOGNIZED-BUT-UNKNOWN vs. UNRECOGNIZED comparison at held-constant veracity/knowledge, and the synthetic-entity anchor are designed to isolate genuine leakage from valid frequency-based inference (though full separation is difficult). The recognition and knowledge channels may be hard to separate (recognition often co-occurs with knowledge); the recognized-but-unknown cell and projected-out analyses are built to dissociate them, and even a characterization of entanglement is informative and directly engages the 'recall-process-not-truth' finding. The effect may be absent internally — a robust negative result (recognition does not contaminate the truth channel) would itself be a valuable, publishable finding contrasting with the human recognition-based truth effect. Familiarity estimated from subject popularity is noisy; we use multiple frequency proxies and the synthetic anchor. The truth/recognition probes may not be cleanly linear at every layer; we report layerwise results with control tasks. The leak component may be distributed rather than a discrete head; we treat 'steer to decouple recognition from truth' as the causal test rather than pinning an exact head. Steering could degrade fluency or make the model distrust all familiar content; we use small magnitudes, random/truth-direction baselines, and monitor perplexity, known-fact accuracy, and general benchmarks. Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: belief_dilution_effect
Title: Watered Down: Does Irrelevant Information Literally Dilute an LLM's Internal Belief Signal?
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human dilution effect (non-diagnostic information weakens the pull of diagnostic evidence), adding irrelevant, non-diagnostic facts to a context weakens an LLM's internally-decoded belief in a conclusion that its diagnostic evidence supports — the belief regresses toward neutral. We further hypothesize this internal dilution is realized geometrically as a REDUCTION IN MAGNITUDE of the belief signal along the truth direction (a literal 'radial dilution'), not merely an angular rotation, and that it predicts diluted behavioral judgments and is causally reversible by rescaling the belief component.
Related Work: The dilution effect — non-diagnostic information weakening the implications of diagnostic information, yielding less extreme judgments — is a canonical, heavily-cited human finding (Tversky & Kleinman 1981, 611 citations; The Dilution Effect and Perceptual Decision Making 2015; The Moral Dilution Effect 2025; Restoration of Diluted Judgment 2008). A long-standing open debate is whether dilution is genuine dilution of the diagnostic signal or an inference of missing evidence. In LLM interpretability, belief/truth is a linearly-decodable, context-sensitive causal mediator that is even sensitive to IRRELEVANT context (Truth-value judgment: belief directions are context sensitive 2024), belief posteriors form curved manifolds whose mean/variance shift with evidence (The Shape of Beliefs 2026), and 'Simulated Adoption' (2026) provides the crucial geometric framing for in-context conflict as either RADIAL magnitude dilution or ANGULAR orthogonal rotation of the truth direction. CRITICALLY, no work isolates the classic dilution effect as an internal belief phenomenon: whether appending non-diagnostic facts weakens the internal belief in a diagnostically-supported conclusion, whether this is realized as radial magnitude reduction vs. angular rotation, whether it reflects genuine dilution vs. missing-evidence inference, or whether it can be causally reversed by rescaling the belief signal. This transfers a canonical human bias into LLM belief internals and, by importing the radial-vs-angular decomposition from Simulated Adoption, gives it a novel mechanistic, causal treatment distinct from all my prior belief-attribute proposals (which concern repetition, source independence, anchoring, halo, etc., never non-diagnostic dilution).
Abstract: Told that a student scored in the top 5% of a hard exam, people confidently predict she is excellent; add that she owns a cat and jogs on weekends — utterly irrelevant — and their confidence drops. This dilution effect, one of the most reproduced biases in judgment research, has never been examined inside LLMs at the level of their beliefs. As LLMs increasingly reason over long, cluttered contexts (RAG passages padded with irrelevant text, verbose user messages), we ask a sharp mechanistic question: does appending non-diagnostic information weaken the model's internally-decoded belief in a conclusion its diagnostic evidence supports, and if so, how is that weakening realized geometrically? We hypothesize that (i) adding irrelevant facts regresses the internal belief readout toward neutral — an internal dilution effect; (ii) this is realized as a reduction in the MAGNITUDE of the belief signal along the truth direction (radial dilution) rather than an angular rotation of it; (iii) the internal dilution predicts diluted behavioral judgments and grows with the amount of irrelevant material; and (iv) it is causally reversible by rescaling the belief component along the truth direction, restoring undiluted judgments. We build a controlled dataset of diagnostic-evidence items paired with matched non-diagnostic padding (and length-matched diagnostic and neutral-token controls), with a synthetic-entity track to control priors. On frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B) we train linear belief probes, decompose the belief signal into radial and angular components, quantify per-item dilution, test the missing-evidence-inference alternative, localize the responsible heads via activation patching, and test causal rescaling. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, dilution magnitude, radial-vs-angular decomposition, dose-response, dilution-error AUROC, patching effect sizes, post-rescaling restoration, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Generate ~6k judgment items each with a DIAGNOSTIC evidence statement that strongly supports a conclusion C about an item (e.g., 'Alex scored in the top 2% on a rigorous certification exam' -> 'Alex is highly competent'; entity-attribute inferences). Two tracks: (a) REAL items; (b) a SYNTHETIC novel-entity track (invented people/objects/attributes) to control pretraining priors and stipulate diagnosticity. For each item, construct matched conditions holding the diagnostic evidence constant: (i) DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY baseline; (ii) DILUTED — the diagnostic evidence PLUS k non-diagnostic facts about the same item (irrelevant hobbies, unrelated demographics), at graded amounts k in {1,2,4,8}; controls: (iii) LENGTH-MATCHED NEUTRAL padding (topically-unrelated filler not about the item, controls for pure context length); (iv) EXTRA-DIAGNOSTIC (adding a second genuinely relevant fact, which should NOT dilute and may strengthen); (v) a MISSING-EVIDENCE-CUE variant where the non-diagnostic facts are framed as an exhaustive dossier ('here is everything known about Alex') vs. an incidental aside, to test the inference-of-missing-evidence account (dilution should be larger when the padding implies the diagnostic fact is all-there-is). Add a behavioral JUDGMENT probe ('How confident are you that C? 0-100'), comprehension checks (can the model identify which facts are relevant), and paraphrase/order perturbations. Human-validate diagnosticity/non-diagnosticity labels on a sample. 2) Belief probing: For Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, extract residual-stream and per-head activations at the conclusion's key tokens across layers, WITHOUT asking the judgment question. Train a linear BELIEF probe (P(C holds), graded) with shuffled-label control tasks; report per-layer accuracy/AUROC. 3) Dilution measurement (key test): Define per-item dilution = belief(DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY) - belief(DILUTED), i.e. regression of the belief readout toward neutral. Test dilution > 0 across models, domains, and tracks versus the rational null (irrelevant facts should not change belief); confirm the LENGTH-MATCHED NEUTRAL control does NOT produce the same regression (so dilution is driven by non-diagnostic facts ABOUT THE ITEM, not context length), and that EXTRA-DIAGNOSTIC does not dilute. Fit a dose-response of dilution vs. k. Compare internal dilution to behavioral judgment dilution (verbal dilution effect). 4) Radial-vs-angular geometry (mechanistic key test): Following the Simulated Adoption decomposition, project the conclusion representation onto the truth/belief direction and decompose the change under dilution into a RADIAL component (magnitude reduction along the truth direction) and an ANGULAR component (rotation away from the truth direction). Test whether dilution is dominated by radial magnitude loss (literal 'watering down') vs. angular displacement, per model and layer. 5) Missing-evidence-inference test: Compare dilution in the exhaustive-dossier vs. incidental-aside framings (condition v). A larger dilution under the exhaustive framing supports the inference-of-missing-evidence account; equal dilution supports genuine signal dilution — adjudicating the long-standing human-literature debate inside the model. 6) Predictiveness: Test whether internal dilution (read before the query) predicts per-item behavioral judgment regression via correlation/AUROC, beyond a log-prob baseline and beyond context length. 7) Localization: Use activation patching / causal mediation from DILUTED to DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY runs to find heads/layers that carry the diluted (attenuated) belief signal; contrast with truth/belief heads and with heads that attend to the non-diagnostic tokens. 8) Causal control: Derive the truth direction (difference-in-means) and test a geometry-aware RESCALING intervention — amplify the radial belief component along the truth direction under dilution. Test (a) rescaling restores undiluted belief and behavioral judgments; (b) suppressing it exaggerates dilution; (c) specificity: random-direction and pure-angular steering do not selectively restore the belief; (d) collateral checks on general benchmarks (MMLU subset), diagnostic-only accuracy, and perplexity. 9) Generalization: Test probe/rescaling transfer across domains (competence judgments, entity attributes, prediction tasks), real vs. synthetic tracks, and dilution amounts. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, dilution magnitude and dose-response, radial-vs-angular decomposition shares, length-control and extra-diagnostic specificity, exhaustive-vs-incidental framing contrast, dilution-error AUROC (vs. log-prob and length baselines), patching logit-difference effect sizes, post-rescaling restoration and specificity, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The regression toward neutral could reflect generic context-length effects or attention diffusion rather than a specific non-diagnostic-dilution phenomenon; the LENGTH-MATCHED NEUTRAL control (irrelevant filler NOT about the item), the EXTRA-DIAGNOSTIC control, and the requirement that dilution be driven by item-specific non-diagnostic facts are designed to dissociate genuine dilution from length/diffusion artifacts. The effect may be absent internally — a robust negative result (LLMs ignore non-diagnostic facts and preserve the belief signal) would itself be a valuable, publishable finding contrasting with the canonical human bias and reassuring for cluttered-context deployment. The genuine-dilution vs. missing-evidence-inference distinction may not fully resolve; the exhaustive-vs-incidental framing test provides evidence but, as in the human literature, may be only partially conclusive — still an informative contribution to a decades-old debate. The graded belief probe requires calibration; we anchor on diagnostic-only items with known belief and report layerwise results with control tasks, focusing on relative change. The radial-vs-angular decomposition depends on a well-estimated truth direction; we use difference-in-means with cross-validation and report per-layer results, and note architectures may differ (Simulated Adoption found norm dynamics vary by model). Rescaling could degrade fluency or over-amplify belief indiscriminately; we use small magnitudes, random/angular-direction baselines, and monitor perplexity, diagnostic-only accuracy, and general benchmarks. Diagnosticity labels are partly subjective; we human-validate a sample. Results may not transfer to very large closed models.

Name: belief_rigidity_ontogeny
Title: Learning to Be Stubborn: The Developmental Emergence of Belief Entrenchment Across Pretraining
Short Hypothesis: As a language model pretrains and a fact's parametric belief strengthens, the model's willingness to OVERRIDE that belief with in-context counter-evidence progressively DECAYS: per-fact, the pretraining checkpoint at which a belief becomes linearly decodable predicts the checkpoint at which that belief becomes context-unrevisable. Belief entrenchment (the failure of RAG-style in-context correction) is thus an emergent ontogenetic property that co-develops with, and is causally tied to, parametric belief consolidation rather than being a fixed trait of the final model.
Related Work: Pretraining-dynamics work characterizes WHEN factual knowledge is acquired and forgotten (How Do LLMs Acquire Factual Knowledge 2024; How do LMs learn facts 2025 - three-phase plateau; Probing Across Time 2021), that linear representations of relations form at frequency thresholds (On Linear Representations and Pretraining Data Frequency 2025), and that KNOWLEDGE ENTROPY decays over pretraining, impairing new-knowledge integration (Knowledge Entropy Decay 2024). Component-evolution work tracks head/FFN specialization over training (Time Course MechInterp 2025; Crosscoding Through Time 2025). Inference-time work shows final models over-rely on parametric priors and resist in-context correction (context-vs-prior conflict, RAG faithfulness). CRITICALLY, none link the two: no work asks whether, per individual fact, the emergence of a decodable parametric belief CAUSES the loss of in-context revisability (belief entrenchment), nor traces this acquisition-to-rigidity tradeoff across checkpoints, nor tests whether the same mechanism (e.g. knowledge-entropy decay / consolidated recall circuits) that consolidates the belief is what makes it unrevisable. This reframes belief entrenchment as a developmental phenomenon with a per-fact ontogenetic timeline, distinct from acquisition/forgetting dynamics (which ignore in-context override) and from my prior inference-time-only belief proposals.
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented and correction-based systems assume a model will update its answer when the context contradicts what it knows. Yet models notoriously cling to their parametric priors. We ask a developmental question that prior pretraining-dynamics work has not: does a fact's belief become HARDER to override with in-context counter-evidence as the model learns it more strongly, and are these two timelines causally linked? We hypothesize that (i) for a given fact, there is a checkpoint at which its parametric belief becomes linearly decodable (acquisition) and a later checkpoint at which the model stops revising that belief when the context asserts the opposite (entrenchment); (ii) per-fact acquisition timing predicts entrenchment timing, so belief rigidity co-develops with consolidation rather than being uniform across the final model; and (iii) the consolidation mechanism (a strengthening parametric-recall circuit and declining reliance on context) causally drives the loss of revisability, so that intervening on it restores in-context updatability. Using open pretraining checkpoints (Pythia suite, OLMo-7B) with known training-data frequencies, we build controlled fact sets, present each fact under a matched in-context contradiction, and at each checkpoint measure (a) parametric belief via a linear probe, (b) in-context revision behavior, and (c) an internal 'context-vs-prior reliance' signal. We trace per-fact acquisition and entrenchment curves, test their predictive coupling against frequency and difficulty baselines, localize the consolidating recall component, and causally test whether attenuating it re-opens in-context revisability. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, per-fact acquisition/entrenchment checkpoints and their correlation, revision-rate trajectories, coupling AUROC vs. baselines, patching/ablation effect sizes, post-intervention revision restoration, and perplexity.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Assemble ~4k subject-relation-object facts spanning a wide range of pretraining-corpus frequencies (using published OLMo/Pythia term-frequency estimates), plus a matched difficulty control set. For each fact, construct (a) a closed-book PARAMETRIC query ('The capital of X is ___'), and (b) an IN-CONTEXT CONTRADICTION prompt asserting the opposite value ('Document: The capital of X is [wrong value]. Question: What is the capital of X?') with matched wording, so a context-faithful model would return the contradicted value. Include a NEUTRAL-context control (context restates the true value or is irrelevant) and comprehension checks (can the model quote the context value). 2) Checkpoint sweep: Use the Pythia suite (multiple sizes: 160M, 1.4B, 6.9B) across its released checkpoints and OLMo-7B intermediate checkpoints. At each checkpoint, for each fact measure: (i) PARAMETRIC BELIEF via a linear probe on residual-stream activations at the object token (trained per-checkpoint with shuffled-label control tasks) and via closed-book log-prob; (ii) IN-CONTEXT REVISION behavior = does the model output the contradicted context value vs. its parametric value; (iii) an internal CONTEXT-vs-PRIOR reliance signal (a linear probe / logit-lens measure of whether the answer token is driven by context tokens vs. the parametric recall pathway, e.g. via attention-to-context and activation-patching-based attribution). 3) Ontogeny curves (key test): Per fact, define the ACQUISITION checkpoint (first checkpoint where parametric belief probe crosses a criterion) and the ENTRENCHMENT checkpoint (first checkpoint where in-context revision rate drops below a criterion, i.e. the model stops accepting the contradiction). Test the coupling hypothesis: acquisition checkpoint predicts entrenchment checkpoint (per-fact correlation), and entrenchment lags acquisition by a characteristic interval. Test whether high-frequency facts entrench earlier. 4) Predictiveness against baselines: Test whether per-fact parametric belief strength at a given checkpoint predicts subsequent loss of in-context revisability (AUROC), beyond corpus frequency and beyond a difficulty baseline (partial regression), isolating the belief-consolidation contribution. 5) Localization: At a mid/late checkpoint, use activation patching / attention attribution to identify the parametric-recall component (heads/FFNs) that carries the entrenched belief and suppresses context reliance; compare across checkpoints to see this component strengthen as entrenchment sets in (linking to Time Course MechInterp / knowledge-entropy findings). 6) Causal intervention: On late (entrenched) checkpoints, test whether attenuating the recall component (ablation / down-scaling its contribution, or steering along a 'context-reliance' direction derived contrastively from early-vs-late or revised-vs-unrevised activations) RESTORES in-context revision on contradicted facts. Report (a) revision-rate recovery, (b) specificity: random-component ablation and neutral-context accuracy preserved, (c) collateral checks on general benchmarks (subset) and perplexity. 7) Generalization: Test that acquisition->entrenchment coupling and the intervention transfer across model sizes, relation types, and frequency bands. Metrics: probe accuracy/AUROC, per-fact acquisition/entrenchment checkpoint distributions and their correlation, revision-rate trajectories over checkpoints, entrenchment-prediction AUROC vs. frequency/difficulty baselines, patching/ablation logit-difference effect sizes, component-strength-over-training curves, post-intervention revision restoration and specificity, perplexity/benchmark deltas.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Entrenchment could simply track corpus frequency rather than a distinct consolidation-to-rigidity mechanism; the frequency-matched difficulty controls and the partial-regression predictiveness test (belief strength beyond frequency) are designed to isolate the belief-consolidation contribution. The acquisition-then-entrenchment ordering may not hold for all facts, or the two timelines may be inseparable (a fact might be revisable and unlearned, or entrenched from first acquisition) - a robust finding either way (coupled vs. decoupled ontogeny) is informative and publishable. In-context revision behavior depends on prompt scaffolding and could reflect instruction-following rather than belief rigidity; comprehension checks, neutral-context controls, and multiple contradiction phrasings mitigate this, though base (non-instruct) checkpoints may under-follow context, which we treat as part of the developmental signal and compare across contradiction strengths. The linear belief probe may not be cleanly decodable or comparable across checkpoints (representations drift); we retrain probes per-checkpoint with control tasks and corroborate with log-prob measures. The recall component may be distributed rather than a discrete head; we treat 'attenuate to restore revisability' as the causal test rather than pinning an exact unit. Checkpoint availability limits us to Pythia/OLMo (specific data mixes); results may not transfer to other pretraining regimes or to very large closed models. Restoring context-reliance via intervention could degrade fluency or make the model indiscriminately gullible to any context; we use small magnitudes, random-component baselines, and monitor perplexity, neutral-context accuracy, and general benchmarks.
